_provenance.derived_from: 168 Cambridge published mark schemes, 2020-2025 (84 x 0450, 84 x 0455)
_provenance.derivation_policy: structure only. No mark-scheme wording is reproduced in learner-facing output.
_provenance.validation: per-paper tariff sums reconcile: 0450 = 80; 0455 Paper 2 = 110 printed (30 Section A + 4 x 20 Section B, candidate answers three, for 90).
_provenance.verification: Every shape below was re-counted against the raw mark-scheme text, per question block, not per file. The percentage on each shape is the share of that command-word-and-tariff population that carries the stated structure. A shape under 90% carries its exceptions.

0450.subject: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies

shapes.guard: an example is not a definition
only the first two responses are marked

shape: or 2 items each with a context reference
each: 1 mark for the point + 1 mark for a relevant reference to the named business
shapes.guard: answers must address the party the question names, not another stakeholder
shapes.verified: 95% award a mark per point plus a mark per relevant reference to the named business, giving 2 x (point + application).

shape: each: identification of the point + a reference that works the point through the named business + the consequence that follows
shapes.caps: max two of each mark type
shapes.context_required: on a question that names a business, yes
shapes.note: the single most common question form in Paper 1: a 2 x 3 grid
shapes.guard: Naming a context word is not application. The mark is for the point being worked through that context. Examiners refuse a context word used as decoration in 27 separate statements.
shapes.verified: 141 of 202 (70%) carry all three mark types. Of the rest, 18% carry identification + explanation with no application mark and 12% carry application + explanation. The missing mark is almost always application, on a question written without a case context.

shapes.note: own-figure rule applies: a correct method on a wrong earlier figure still earns the method mark

shape: one mark for each distinct relevant point, capped (max two or max four)
one further mark for each point that is developed to its consequence
shapes.verified: 94% state a cap on the number of points; 99% award development marks separately. Only 16% award a separate application mark, so unlike the 6-mark Explain this is a point-and-development question, not a point-context-consequence one.
shapes.note: Paper 2. Four of these carry 32 of the paper’s 80 marks.

requires: sound application of knowledge and understanding of relevant business concepts using appropriate terminology
detailed discussion of two or more of the named options
bands.top_of_band: all named options discussed in detail and in context, with an explicit statement of why the rejected options were rejected

requires: detailed discussion of at least one option

shapes.note: 48 of Paper 2's 80 marks. The band-3 ceiling turns on rejecting the alternatives explicitly.
shapes.verified: 100% are level-banded over three bands. 99% require a well-justified recommendation or conclusion for the top band. 94% reserve the ceiling of the top band for candidates who also say why the rejected options were rejected — the single most reliable finding in the whole corpus, and the one examiner reports most often say candidates miss.

refusals: naming a context word from the case does not earn the application mark; the point has to be worked through in that context
an example is not a definition and is not an explanation
an answer written from the wrong stakeholder's point of view scores nothing
a solution offered where the question asked for a cause or an effect scores nothing
a point restated in different words is not a second point
